parts.text: By contrast, we found no statistically significant differences in early adulthood poverty between the income group just below the

and those who grew up in households with higher incomes.

A ‘double whammy’ for kids from single-parent families

Australia has 1.2 million single parent families. Children in those families are especially vulnerable to poverty persisting into early adulthood.

to 2026 ACOSS–UNSW research, 37% of children in sole-parent families were living in poverty in 2022–23, compared with 11% of children in partnered families.

Low-income single-parent families face compounding pressures: even beyond obvious financial pressures, one parent also has to carry out all the

work of child care and household tasks.

Not only are children in single-parent families more likely to experience poverty, our research showed that poverty is more

into adulthood, likely because of those compounding pressures. It’s a double whammy.

In August 2025, Swinburne University researchers surveyed 2,590 Australian single parents, who were mostly women.

They found almost four out of five single mothers (78%) spent “a lot” or “almost all” of their time worrying about or planning for their family’s financial

. As one respondent said:

I need more money. The financial stress feels untenable.

What makes poverty persist into adulthood?

We examined several possible reasons why poverty is more likely to last into later life. These included educational attainment, reduced

, lower rates of partnering and poorer health.

We found people who grew up in more disadvantaged households were generally less likely to complete post-school qualifications, be employed or live with a partner.

They were also more likely to be single parents. Some health measures were also

with childhood economic circumstances.

These adult outcomes are themselves associated with poverty risk. But even when we accounted for them, the association between childhood poverty and early-adulthood poverty remained

.

What can we do about it?

Our research doesn’t isolate a single cause of childhood poverty. But our findings do strongly suggest policies focused on reducing poverty in families with children can deliver lasting benefits.

To significantly reduce adult poverty, we need more focus on directly reducing economic

in families with children, especially those from low-income single-parent families.

In 2023, the Albanese government boosted financial support for low-income single parents, raising the age cut-off for the Parenting
(Single) until the youngest child turns 14. That change was expected to help at least 57,000 single primary carers, who were mostly women (91%).

reading.title: 主旨、理解与信息定位
reading.instruction: 阅读原文后回答 5 道选择题：1 道主旨、1 道内容理解、1 道段落细节、2 道信息定位。段落细节题以题干指定段落为准。

questions.prompt: Which statement best summarises the overall focus of this article?
options: Data-centre development is associated with modest local employment growth rather than a jobs boom.
Fireworks create environmental and economic costs that outlast the celebrations.
Long-term evidence shows how childhood poverty can continue to shape economic disadvantage in adulthood.
Resilience beyond short household emergencies depends on stronger food supply chains.
questions.explanation: 把标题与全文各段的中心内容连起来判断主旨，避免把同一主题下的其他话题当成本文重点。
questions.evidence: Our research, recently published in The Economic Record, suggests childhood poverty casts a long shadow, affecting young Australians well into their 20s and 30s.

questions.prompt: What makes the HILDA data useful for studying long-term poverty?
options: It follows Australian households over time, beginning in 2001.
It records only one day's purchases at one shop.
It excludes all information about households.
It contains only anonymous film reviews.
questions.explanation: 第 6 段提供了作答依据。正确选项用不同说法表达了文中的信息；请比较范围、数量、因果关系与限定词。
questions.evidence: We used data from the Household, Income and Labour Dynamics in Australia (HILDA) Survey, which has followed Australian households since 2001.

questions.prompt: Which of the following statements is explicitly made in paragraph 12?
options: That’s about one in six Australian children, according to the latest estimates from the Australian Council of Social Service (ACOSS) and UNSW Sydney.

We found children growing up below the poverty line had a 22.4 percentage points higher risk of living in poverty in their 20s and early 30s than those who grew up in households with incomes between 150% and 200% of the poverty line.
What this means is that Australians who grow up poor face a 27% risk of being in poverty in early adulthood, in contrast to just 5% in the reference group.
We examined several possible reasons why poverty is more likely to last into later life.
questions.explanation: 定位第 12 段，比较四个选项的具体信息。其余选项来自本文其他段落，并非本段明确陈述的内容。
questions.evidence: What this means is that Australians who grow up poor face a 27% risk of being in poverty in early adulthood, in contrast to just 5% in the reference group.
